summary: Former Soviet collective-farm manager Alexander Lukashenko won Belarus's 1994 presidential election on an anti-corruption platform, then gutted parliament, rigged elections and jailed or disappeared opponents for over 26 years.
keywords: Union State of Russia and Belarus

evidence.note: birth date given as 30 August 1954; birthplace disputed in his own accounts
long segment on shifting state-made biographies and folklore-style propaganda about him
1994 presidential run and win on anti-corruption platform; chosen as main_span start
fight with parliament, 1995 elections stifled, 1996 constitutional change makes him a dictator
Soviet-style collectivised economy kept afloat by cheap Russian oil
balancing between Russia and the West, sanctions after 2006, gas price disputes
COVID-19 denial, his own infection, citizens crowdfunding medical supplies
2020 election: opposition candidates jailed, Tsikhanouskaya campaign, rigged result
audio of detained protesters being tortured is played and discussed

notes: Part 1 opens with a long survey of Belarusian history (Polotsk, Grand Duchy of Lithuania, world wars), treated as background and excluded from covered_span. RU is in setting for the Russia relationship and treaties rather than events on Russian soil. Torture warning rests on a short but vivid audio clip; reviewer may drop it.
